Latency SLOs and recent p95 regressions

transcript:
[00:00] Avery (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time for the QBR style checkpoint. quick roll call?
[00:10] Priya (Head of ML): Priya here, Daniel, Sara, Owen on from our side.
[00:14] Daniel (CTO): yep hi all.
[00:18] Lina (CSM): Lina from Redwood, thanks all.
[00:22] Miguel (SE): Miguel here — hey.
[01:15] Priya: ok so high level - usage has grown about 3.4x since January, a lot of that is interactive chat sessions. we've seen p95 latency creep during peaks, which hit our customer-facing flows. we wanted to align on cost and runway and see what a pilot for dedicated looks like.
[01:40] Avery: yeah that’s the call. maybe start with the usage profile Sara — can you summarize traffic shapes?
[01:51] Sara: sure — day to day baseline about 600 qps tokens, spikes up to 1.8k during promo pushes, 45% of calls are multi-turn chat with long contexts, average request size ~3.2k tokens, tail is heavy because of embeddings pipelines too.
[02:20] Miguel: couple of quick notes — long contexts mean we should be leveraging prefix/KV cache aggressively, and we can change batching windows for typical 200-400ms latency targets to save cost. but with those spike windows you may want burst capacity.
[02:42] Owen (Finance): cost is the big question. our forecast assumes current hosted spend grows linearly, but with 3x usage we're looking at a 2.8x budget unless we commit. what's the delta to Dedicated?
[03:00] Avery: (laughs) math time. we have a new pilot pricing worksheet. summary: Dedicated monthly commit tends to reduce per-token cost by ~30-45% depending on utilization and model size. but there's a capex/commitment trade — if you can't commit we can do hybrid routing: host for baseline, dedicated for sustained, automatic fallback.
[03:30] Priya: curious about model variants — can we pin to a quantized variant for bulk inference and use full precision for small high-value flows?
[03:41] Miguel: yes. Redwood supports model variants and automated routing so you can route by route type. quantization profiles we've recommended for similar workloads have cut token compute by ~2.2x in our tests, though you need evals for quality.
[04:05] Daniel: last week we had two p95 spikes at 23:12 and 23:37, roughly 12 minutes apart, they correlated with a campaign and an ingestion batch. our ops oncall saw backpressure in the gateway.
[04:23] Sara: logs show KV cache misses during that period because many sessions started with fresh contexts. also backend ingestion hit DB and delayed response fanout.
[04:33] Miguel: that makes sense — cool optimization is pre-warming prefixes for campaign-driven sessions and using short-lived reserved slots in Dedicated during the planned push. that avoids cold kv miss tax.
[05:00] Priya: is pre-warming something Redwood can orchestrate or is it ops work on our side?
[05:07] Lina: there are two patterns — you can push warm-up requests from your side or we can schedule a short pre-warm job if on Dedicated. we'll document recommended patterns.
[05:30] Owen: procurement question — what SLAs do we get on Dedicated?
[05:38] Avery: SLA is SLA-backed for Dedicated: 99.9% availability target and latency windows we can commit to in the contract based on profile. we'll include specifics in the pilot paperwork.
[06:00] Priya: security — we need SOC2 + data residency and KMS support. we've got a security review coming next month.
[06:10] Miguel: Redwood Private and Dedicated both support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and VPC peering options. we also have audit logs and retention controls. I'll attach the SOC2 + short FAQ with answers to the usual questions.
[06:30] Daniel: any gotchas around KV cache and PII? we store short lived session metadata.
[06:36] Miguel: KV cache is in-memory on the serving nodes; for Private deployments you can configure policies for retention and encryption. default hosted cache is ephemeral and not persisted beyond SLO window.
[07:00] Priya: on model quality — can we run a quality regression test when you quantize? we need automated evals tied to our prompt sets.
[07:12] Miguel: yes — Redwood Optimize integrates with eval harnesses. we can run A/B against your prompts and generate diff reports. quality alerts can be wired to the console.
[07:40] Sara: what about canaries and rollbacks — we had a bad rollout in-house and want a safe path.
[07:48] Lina: built-in rollouts: canary percentage, automatic rollback on quality regression or latency regress, and route-based fallback to a stable variant. you can set thresholds.
[08:05] Owen: cost simulation — can you show cost with caching enabled vs disabled?
[08:12] Miguel: yes that's exactly part of the benchmark. I'll produce two sims: (1) hosted baseline with current traffic, (2) dedicated with 8:1 commit utilization, with KV cache and quantized model savings layered on.
[08:40] Priya: success criteria for pilot: p95 under 700ms for interactive flows, under 200ms for system-to-system embedding lookups, 25% reduction in per-token compute cost net of commits, and no quality drop greater than 1.5% on our eval NPS metric.
[09:03] Avery: that’s perfect — we'll formalize in the pilot doc.
[09:20] Speaker 1 (intern): quick question — do we keep logs for 90 days or can we shorten?
[09:25] Miguel: retention configurable; you can set a retention policy, and export logs to your SIEM for longer-term.
[09:40] Daniel: on the latency incident notes — can Redwood trace correlation ids through to the model-level logs? we want end-to-end observability.
[09:48] Miguel: yes, we instrument request ids and per-token timing slices. the console shows per-route token-time breakdown and KV hit/miss metrics. we can add your correlation id header to traces.
[10:10] Priya: will the quantized variant affect beam search/topk behaviour? we've seen hallucination patterns with aggressive quant.
[10:20] Miguel: it can, depends on model and quant scheme. that's why we always run evals and compare distributions for logits, topk stability. our recommendation is to stage quant at 8-bit first, run A/B, then decide.
[10:50] Sara: can we test our embeddings pipeline — current job spikes the cluster because we do batch embedding for cold recall updates.
[10:58] Miguel: batching window tuning and moving large batch jobs to off-peak or background dedicated slot helps. another pattern is to have separate dedicated pool for heavy embedding throughput.
[11:20] Owen: also need a clear forecast for finance — give us 3 scenarios: conservative, expected, aggressive with breakdown of token classes and forecasted savings with Dedicated.
[11:32] Avery: we'll include those three scenarios in the worksheet — Miguel will supply assumptions.
[12:00] Priya: timeline — we'd like pilot to start May 10, run 4 weeks, then exec review with finance to decide on commit for H2. is that plausible?
[12:10] Miguel: yes that timeline works; micro-setup for Dedicated can take 3-7 business days if nothing custom.
[12:22] Daniel: procurement lead time could be 4 weeks, so sooner we get paper the better.
[12:30] Lina: I'll schedule the exec recap for week after pilot completes and coordinate with Owen on availability.
[13:00] Priya: another quick ask — can we get a short whitepaper on model pinning guarantees and rollback SLAs for private deployments?
[13:08] Avery: yep we'll send a short one pager plus the SLA excerpts.
[13:30] Speaker 1: small note — does Redwood offer training credits or onboarding help for infra team?
[13:37] Lina: yes we include onboarding hours, and for Dedicated there is an onboarding package available as add-on. we'll outline it in the pricing doc.
[14:05] Miguel: i'm going to call out the experiments we recommend during pilot: (1) baseline hosted with KV cache off, (2) hosted with cache on, (3) dedicated unquantized, (4) dedicated quantized 8-bit. for each run we'll capture cost per 1k tokens, p50/p95/p99 latencies, kv hit rates, and quality diffs.
[14:40] Priya: that matrix is helpful. for quality diffs we need top-level metrics plus a small custom prompt set of 250 queries.
[14:50] Miguel: noted.
[15:10] Daniel: on-canary behaviour — if a canary fails at 10% do you automatically rollback or pause?
[15:17] Lina: configurable. default is auto-rollback on threshold breach or pause with alert to operators. you can also set manual gating.
[15:40] Owen: are there termination fees if we don't hit committed utilization?
[15:46] Avery: there's a commitment clause; we can structure a ramped commit or a smaller pilot commit. termination depends on contract language — we'll surface options.
[16:00] Priya: security review dates — our info sec team needs to meet, can you make next week?
[16:05] Miguel: yes Miguel + Lina can be available. we'll prepare SOC2 artifacts and the KMS/HSM config note.
[16:30] Sara: small ops question — what's the behavior when a node OOMs during heavy embedding batch? do requests fallback gracefully?
[16:37] Miguel: runtime has automatic routing to healthy workers and capacity-aware scheduling; on Dedicated we allocate headroom and can spill to host fallback if configured. fallbacks are configurable per-route.
[17:00] Priya: do you collect per-user or per-organization quotas? we may want rate limits per-tenant in a multi-tenant flow.
[17:07] Miguel: yes we have per-token rate limiting, route-level quotas, and token-level cost attribution in the console.
[17:30] Daniel: can we get the console demo for our infra team during the pilot?
[17:35] Lina: absolutely, we'll schedule a 45 min SE-led walkthrough for the ops team.
[18:00] Owen: will you include a simple cashflow model that shows payback period on commit?
[18:06] Avery: yes we'll include payback curve and sensitivity to utilization.
[18:30] Priya: anything else from Redwood?
[18:35] Miguel: just to confirm deliverables: benchmark runs and artifact, quant eval, pricing worksheet, SOC2 bundle, and one-pager on rollback/SLA.
[18:45] Avery: and we'll do the exec recap after pilot.
[19:00] Sara: on our side we'll prepare the 30-day logs and the 250-prompt eval set.
[19:10] Priya: and we'll loop in security.
[19:20] Owen: finance will review the worksheet and we should have a decision window within 2 weeks of pilot completion.
[19:40] Avery: great, that's actionable. Lina will send calendar invites and next steps. thanks everyone.
[19:55] Daniel: thanks all.
[20:05] (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains some auto-attrib errors (Speaker 1 is an intern), occasional mis-hearings: "KV miss tax" recorded literally. Several sections where product names are truncated or mis-typed in the transcription (e.g., Redwood Dedicate, Redwood Opti). The team used shorthand for p95/p50/p99 and committed utilization.
